Evaluate ${\int }_{C}(\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi y}{2})+{x}^{2})\,\text{d}y,$ where $C$ is the path traversed along the line segment from the point $(2,0)$ to the point $(2,2),$ as shown above.
feedback.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y={\int }_{a}^{b}f(r(t))\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t.
$$

The curve $C$ is a line segment with endpoints $(2,0)$ and $(2,2).$ It can be parametrized as 

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨(2+t(2-2)),\,(0+t(2-0))⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,2t⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

where $0\le t\le 1.$

Computing $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t},$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)=2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y)=\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi y}{2})+{x}^{2}$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi (2t)}{2})+(2)^{2} \\  & =\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡\pi t+4.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now evaluate the integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}f(r(t))\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡\pi t+4)\cdot 2\cdot \text{d}t \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{1}(4+\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡\pi t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =2(4t-\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi t){|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =2[(4-\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi )-(0-\operatorname{cos}⁡0)] \\  & =2[4-(-1)+1] \\  & =12\end{aligned}
$$
